title: How Airbnb uses cost per task to operate coding agents on Amazon Bedrock
summary: Airbnb runs evals on real engineering tasks and uses Amazon Bedrock observability to choose models for its coding agents and control production costs. This post shows how cost per task guides model selection, why production spending can differ from eval results, and how to monito
reason: Customer case study on cost-per-task model selection for coding agents on Bedrock: no named model release, no research artifact, no business event (financing/M&A/partnership/product launch), no policy action, no OSS tool release. No rule covers it.
